title: Indian Food Fair Returns to Salt Lake City's Liberty Park on August 15 for Independence Day Celebration
excerpt: The annual community event organized by the Indian Association of Utah will feature traditional cuisine, cultural performances, and Independence Day festivities in one of the state's largest Indian-American gatherings.
body:
• The Indian Food Fair returns to Liberty Park in Salt Lake City on August 15, 2026, coinciding with India's Independence Day celebrations.
  • Organized by the Indian Association of Utah, the event features traditional Indian cuisine from multiple regional traditions, cultural performances, and community activities.
  • Utah's Indian-American population has grown steadily in recent years, driven by the state's expanding tech sector and proximity to companies in the Silicon Slopes corridor.

The Indian Food Fair will return to Liberty Park in Salt Lake City on August 15, 2026, marking India's Independence Day with one of the largest Indian-American community gatherings in the Intermountain West.

Organized by the Indian Association of Utah, the annual event brings together families from across the state and surrounding region for a day of traditional Indian cuisine, cultural performances, and Independence Day festivities. The fair has grown steadily over the past decade as Utah's Indian-American population has expanded, driven by the state's booming tech sector and the cluster of companies along the Silicon Slopes corridor from Lehi to Salt Lake City.

What to Expect

The fair typically features food stalls representing India's diverse regional cuisines — from South Indian dosas and North Indian chaat to Gujarati snacks and Indo-Chinese fusion. Cultural performances include classical and Bollywood dance, live music, and activities for children.

Liberty Park, one of Salt Lake City's oldest and largest public parks, provides a central and accessible venue for the event, with ample green space for the hundreds of families who typically attend.
nri_angle: An annual anchor event for Utah's Indian-American community, drawing families from across the Intermountain West for Independence Day celebrations and community connection.
author: Diaspora Desk
